title: SCE Mesh checkpoint (wire schema v1)
description: A machine's checkpoint on a Mesh host core (SCE_MESH.md section 10.11; docs/adr/0045, section 4; docs/adr/0107, D5): the machine's saved tree and the state of every endpoint in it, one document a host writes in one durable write and a restore reads back. The saved tree is an sce-saved-state text (sce-saved-state.v4.schema.json), held as its JSON value. Every 64-bit number is the text of its digits, every envelope and id the lowercase hexadecimal of its bytes, and every moment milliseconds since the Unix epoch. A checkpoint holds no key, credential or trust state; a host stores it encrypted at rest. The producer and reader is sce-rust-mesh (backends/rust/mesh/src/checkpoint.rs). The stability status of this surface lives in this header alone — see SCE_WIRE_CONTRACTS.md.

format.description: The format version: 1. A reader refuses a format it does not read, before it reads anything else.

checkpoint.description: Which checkpoint of the machine this is, counted by its host from 1: what each endpoint was sealed with.

clean.description: Taken after the core stopped admitting (an orderly shutdown, its links closed first): its restore raises no RESTORED row.

state.description: The machine's saved state, an sce-saved-state document of format 4 (sce-saved-state.v4.schema.json), the format every backend writes. A restore reads the tree with the saved state's own reader, so a checkpoint written before format 4 holds a tree of format 3 and is read as that format is.

endpoints.description: One section per endpoint of the tree, each under the machine name it speaks for.

followed.description: For each journal the session follows (docs/adr/0114, D4), by its name, the position of the last of its entries the session took in, written with what each entry did: an entry at or below it is a repeat. Absent for a session that follows none.

count.description: A whole number of 64 bits, as the text of its digits.

signed.description: A signed whole number of 64 bits, as the text of its digits, with a '-' when it is negative.

bytes.description: Bytes, as the lowercase hexadecimal of each.

id.description: A 16-byte id (an envelope's id, a request's wire invoke_id), as lowercase hexadecimal.

machine.description: The machine the endpoint speaks for: the source of what it sends.

unreleased.description: The envelopes produced and not yet released, in the order they were produced: a restore releases them.

seq.description: Its sequence number, or null when it carries none.

retries.description: Transmissions waiting out their backoff (SCE_MESH.md section 10.10).

backoff.description: The wait last chosen before jitter, or null before the first.

calls.description: What the endpoint released for its machine that the host had not yet applied, in order.

nextseq.description: The sequence number the next envelope to the peer is stamped with.

queued.description: What waits for the peer's link to become ready, oldest first, with the moment it was admitted.

unacked.description: What a binding with durable receipt sent and the peer has not acknowledged, by sequence number.

received.description: Null unless the peer sends to this machine with durable receipt: then every envelope of its stream numbered at most `held` was admitted, and so was each of `above`.

sender.description: One sender's receive state (SCE_MESH.md sections 10.5 and 10.6).

next.description: The sequence it is expected to send next, or null before its first ordered envelope.

held.description: The envelopes held past an ordering gap, with the moment each arrived.

replies.description: The reply cache (SCE_MESH.md section 10.5): each request of the window with its wire invoke_id and the reply its first copy produced, or null while it is handled.

durable.description: Whether its stream has durable receipt: none of its gaps times out.

records.description: Null unless the sender is an instance of an open machine whose binding receives durably (docs/adr/0113, D5): then the incarnation its records are of, the member's low-water mark the store held, and a completion record of each request taken in at or above it, by its number, with its wire invoke_id when a reply answers it and its reply, or null while it is handled or when it has none.

eventCall.description: An event for the machine, with the _event fields a Mesh event carries (SCE_MESH.md section 10.7).

endCall.description: The end of one start of a Mesh request (SCE_MESH.md section 9.5): done.invoke, or error.invoke when failed; source null for a deadline the requester reached itself.
